To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the abandonment of game parks led to the creation of new wilderness areas, (2) the abandonment of the game parks led to a homogenization of lichen and beetle species composition, (3) fungi were mainly driven by dead wood and abandonment favored their richness, (4) canopy openness was the most important management parameter, and (5) wood pasturing and game keeping could be a good alternative management strategy for biodiversity conservation.

(1) the creation of a new forest wilderness in ancient game parks was only profitable for the studied fungi, and (2) the maintenance of canopy openings and the presence of dead wood were important drivers for biodiversity maintenance in the ancient game parks.

the creation of wilderness from ancient forest pastures is profitable for only some species, and that the management of canopy openness and the presence/absence of veteran trees are the main drivers for the maintenance of biodiversity in the studied taxa.

a new way of managing woodlands that can help to conserve biodiversity in the context of the abandonment of ancient oak woodlands in Central Europe.
the conservation of the biodiversity of ancient forests and their management in a way that maintains biodiversity.
the management history and its effect on the biodiversity of ancient forest habitats, which are of great importance in the context of the European Biodiversity Strategy.

the abandonment of ancient pastures in the wilderness is only a good strategy for fungi.
the abandonment of ancient game parks is only profitable for fungi and that the maintenance of the ancient forest pastures is the best option to maintain the highest biodiversity.
a combination of game keeping, wood pasturing and dead wood retention is the best management option for the maintenance of biodiversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biodiversity is best maintained in ancient forest habitats if they are not abandoned, but are used as ancient game parks or ancient wood pastures.
a management history that maintains canopy openness and the presence and condition of veteran trees is important for biodiversity conservation.
a combination of game management and wood pasturing is a suitable management strategy for maintaining biodiversity in ancient oak woodlands.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a multi-taxa study is necessary to understand the effects of abandonment of a former game park on biodiversity, and that the maintenance of a mosaic of open and closed canopy conditions is the most appropriate way to conserve the biodiversity of ancient oak woodlands.
the maintenance of biodiversity in ancient forest pastures requires the maintenance of canopy openings and the presence of dead wood.
the abandonment of ancient oak woodlands is a threat to the conservation of biodiversity and that management is needed to conserve the diversity of lichens, beetles and fungi.
